135: [edit] One should have the custom on Rosh Hashanah of eating rubia, which is fenugreek, leeks, beets, dates, and gourds. When eating rubia, say "May it be Your will that our merits increase [yirbu]." When eating leeks [karti], say "May our enemies be cut down [yikartu]." When eatingbeets [salka], say "May our enemies disappear [yistalku]." When eating dates [tamrei], say "May our enemies end [yitamu]." When eating dates, say "May our decrees be ripped [yikara] and our merits be read [yikaru] before You." Rem"a: Some have the custom of eating a sweet apple with honey (Tur) and saying "May we have a sweet, new year" (Avudraham). This is the practice. Some eat pomegranates and say "May our merits be plentiful like the pomegranate." It is the custom to eat fatty meat and all sorts of sweet things (Mordechai in Yoma).

[edit] We eat the head of a lamb as if to say "Let us be the head and not the tail," and also as a memory of the ram [that took the place] of Isaac. Rem"a: Some are careful not to eat nuts as "nut" has the same numerical value as "sin." Additionally, they cause excess saliva and phlegm and nullify prayers (Mahari"l). We go to the river to say the verse "You shall toss to the depths of the sea all of our sins..." [Micah 7:19] (Minhgaim). It is also the practice to not nap on Rosh Hashanah (Yerushalmi), this is a good custom.
